card: Skips acquiring cs_main in ProcessOrphanTx when a peer has no orphan transactions queued, checking under m_tx_download_mutex first. Currently, ProcessMessages acquires cs_main unconditionally on every peer handler pass, blocking P2P message processing whenever validation, RPC, or wallet threads hold cs_main. In author benchmarks where cs_main was held for 50 ms, ping handling latency dropped from 50.1 ms to 0.02 ms. The PR is self-contained and related to broader lock-reduction work in #36244.
evidence: Author microbenchmarks show ProcessMessages handling a ping taking 50.1 ms on master when cs_main is held for 50 ms by another thread, dropping to 0.02 ms with this change.
A unit test (process_messages_without_orphan_work) reproduces the block on master and passes with this change.
problem: ProcessMessages routinely calls ProcessOrphanTx on each message-processing pass, acquiring cs_main unconditionally even when a peer has no orphan work. P2P message processing for that peer then blocks whenever validation, RPC, or wallet threads hold cs_main.

risk.why: A race condition or locking bug here could delay orphan transaction processing or cause deadlocks during P2P message handling.

scope_notes: Small two-line change in net_processing.cpp paired with a multithreaded unit test in peerman_tests.cpp.
summary: Check whether a peer has orphan transactions waiting under m_tx_download_mutex before acquiring cs_main in ProcessOrphanTx. When no orphan work is queued, ProcessOrphanTx returns immediately without contending for cs_main. A unit test verifies ProcessMessages completes while cs_main is held elsewhere.
